title: Progressive, Regressive and Proportional Taxes
short: Marginal and average tax rates, and what happens to the average rate as income rises.
trouble: Students think moving into a higher bracket taxes all of their income at the higher rate, so a raise could lower take-home pay. Only the dollars above the threshold face the higher marginal rate.

blocks.html: Taxes are one side of fiscal policy, and how they are built matters too. Two rates describe any tax: the share of your total income you pay, and the rate on your next dollar. Both are percents of a number.

Average tax rate = total tax ÷ income. Marginal tax rate = the tax rate on the next dollar of income. A tax is progressive if the average rate rises with income, regressive if it falls, and proportional (flat) if it stays the same.

Under a bracket system, each rate applies only to the income inside its bracket. Picture buckets stacked on top of each other: your income fills the lowest bucket first, then the next. Only the dollars in the top bucket you reach face the top rate. So moving into a higher bracket raises the tax on the dollars above the line, never on the dollars below it. That is why, under bracket rates, a raise always leaves you with more after-tax income, and why the average rate stays below your marginal rate.

blocks.name: ec-taxbrackets
blocks.cap: A made-up three-bracket income tax. Slide the income and watch only the top slice change rate. The right panel shows the average rate always below the marginal rate.

blocks.title: Tax with brackets
blocks.q: A made-up tax: 10% on income up to \$20,000, 20% from \$20,000 to \$60,000, 30% above \$60,000. Find the tax, the average rate and the marginal rate on \$70,000.
steps: Total tax $= 13{,}000$. Average rate $= \dfrac{13{,}000}{70{,}000} \approx 18.6\%$. Marginal rate: 30%.

blocks.title: Crossing a bracket
blocks.q: Under the same tax, income rises from \$59,000 to \$62,000. Does after-tax income rise?
steps: After-tax income rises by \$2,200. Only the \$2,000 above \$60,000 is taxed at 30%.

blocks.html: In the United States, the federal income tax is progressive. Sales taxes tend to be regressive, because lower-income households spend a larger share of their income. A tax that takes the same fixed dollar amount from everyone is regressive too.

Thinking that moving into a higher bracket taxes all of your income at the higher rate, so a raise could lower take-home pay. Only the dollars above the threshold face the higher marginal rate. Check: compute the tax at both incomes; after-tax income always rises under bracket rates.
